author: Gilthunder
quote: Unfortunately for gta 6 it couldn’t live up to the hype. When playing the game not only do the controls feels as clunky as every other rockstar game but the game prides itself on its “extreme realism” and it does deliver in some areas but realism doesn’t exactly mean fun. The story isn’t enjoyable, it’s boring. Also the driving isn’t fun, and you can’t steal any car you like and you can’t kill anyone and everyone. It feels like a watered down game trying to fit into the times when it’s in a genre that’s meant for total freedom. The main characters make strange decisions and Jason feels very bland not really adding much to a conversation most of the time outside of a few “yeahs”. The relationship mechanic while “optional” is still required to get the “good/cannon ending”. So if you are one of those players who has to get every ending or one of the ones who wants the good ending you’ll be running errands most of the game. Stealing cars in this game is a chore, and the honor system is clunky and strange. As said earlier it feels like a very watered down gta 5 put through a visual enhancer. The world is large but empty in most areas. I’d recommend just buying gta 5 on pc and downloading a few mods. Not to mention all of the day one glitches & bugs. I’ve had trucks fall into the ground, Jason fall through the map, heavy frame rate drops, npcs phasing through each other, for $80 minimum it’s inexcusable. Speaking of, the game targeting 30 fps is not great, the game should at least be locked at 30 or 60 on ps5 pro, but the physics is tied to frame rate which is taught as unacceptable to programmers in college. I refunded my copy after 20 hours, I’m upset that I had to do it but at least I have my $80 back that I can spend on something better.
